title: Dark Chocolate, Raspberry and Champagne Cake
story: The champagne isn't a gimmick, though it does sound like one. It adds acidity that cuts through the cocoa and sugar in a way milk doesn't quite manage. The dried raspberries hold their shape through the whole bake and stay tart. It's the kind of cake that sounds fancier than it is, which is usually the best kind.

items.text: 1 cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
½ cup champagne or dry sparkling wine
Chocolate ganache or buttercream, for frosting

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup cocoa powder, 2 tsp baking powder, and 1 tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat 1 cup room-temperature butter, 1 cup granulated sugar, and 1 cup packed brown sugar together until light and creamy, about 3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look noticeably paler and fluffy. Don't rush this step — it builds the cake's structure.

steps.text: Beat in 4 large eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each before adding the next.
Stir in 2 tsp vanilla extract and ½ cup champagne.
Fold in 1 cup dark chocolate chips and ½ cup dried raspberries.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain — overmixing toughens the crumb.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.

steps.donenessCue: A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with just a few moist crumbs — not wet batter. The top should look set and spring back slightly when pressed.

steps.text: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before finishing.
Once fully cooled, dust with powdered sugar or frost with chocolate ganache or buttercream. Dusting is enough — this cake doesn't need much help.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Use fresh raspberries instead of dried — fold them in gently at the very end. The cake will be more delicate and the pockets of fruit more pronounced.
Make a simple chocolate ganache: heat ½ cup heavy cream until just simmering, pour over ½ cup chopped dark chocolate, let sit 2 minutes, then stir until smooth. Pour over the cooled cake.
Add the zest of 1 orange to the butter mixture — it bridges the chocolate and raspberry in a way that makes both taste more like themselves.
Bake as cupcakes at 350°F for 18–22 minutes. Same batter, more surface area for the powdered sugar.
storage: Store loosely covered at room temperature for up to 3 days, or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. If refrigerated, bring to room temperature before serving — cold cake loses its texture. Freeze unfrosted cake (wrapped tightly) for up to 3 months.
